title: This Frog Hides 90% of Its Blood to Turn See-Through

scenes.text: This frog turns see-through by hiding its own blood.
It's called a glassfrog, and when it sleeps, almost 90 percent of its red blood cells leave its bloodstream.
They pack into the liver, which has a reflective coating that bounces light away.
With the red gone, the frog's belly turns clear, and it nearly vanishes against the leaf.
When it wakes up, the blood floods back, and the frog turns solid again.
A frog that hides in plain sight by hiding its own blood.

description:
This frog turns see-through by hiding its own blood.
A 2022 study in Science found glassfrogs store almost 90 percent of their red blood cells in the liver while they sleep.
Would you rather be see-through or invisible?
first_comment: Which would you pick: see-through skin or night vision?
